title: The factory marks a run record orphaned when Cloudflare reports no Workflow instance for it
description: From #87 (2026-09-28): three factory run records (run_9e40b956, run_2e66e765, run_f15efdfb) sat at 'stopping' with no ticks-run Workflow instance on Cloudflare. The client now reads that as orphaned (only on Cloudflare's explicit 404), but the factory itself never finishes such a record, because it refuses to finish a record when the instance read fails, and a missing instance and a failed read currently share one error path. Separate the two in the factory (a typed not-found from the Workflows binding, not error-text matching), then sweep: a record whose instance is definitively absent becomes failed/orphaned, and releases any project lease it holds. Verify whether a frozen 'stopping' record holds the lease today and blocks ticfac run --cloud.
acceptance_criteria: A vitest test: a record with no Workflow instance is finished as orphaned and its lease released; a record whose instance read fails transiently is left alone
closed_reason: Factory sweep (cloudflare/src/run-orphans.ts): the hourly cron finishes a live record whose Workflow instance is complete/errored/terminated or absent (the platform's instance.not_found, read once in readRunInstance) — stopping->stopped, else failed — revokes its tokens, stamps the reason in run_progress, logs finished:<state>, and releases a lease it still holds (RunRoom.releaseLeaseOfEndedRun); a failed read leaves the record and lease alone. stopRun now treats an absent instance as an ended supervisor too. Lease question: a frozen record does not hold the lease beyond its ttl — the RunRoom alarm expires it (the three 72y ghosts showed lease null); it did block the 0.x app deletion (legacyapp.go counts live records). Tests: cloudflare/test/run-orphans.test.ts.
